claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have a child (or children) that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a child - my son Alex. He's 18 and lives at home with me. I was wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few questions.

Since Alex is 18, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not. He finished school and he's not doing any courses or training at the moment. He's just been looking for work really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more questions to ensure I have all the information needed.

Are you responsible for Alex - meaning, does he live with you and do you contribute to the costs of supporting him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives here at home with me and I support him - you know, I pay for his food, his clothes, everything he needs while he's looking for work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

First, are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And finally, are there any other circumstances I should know about? For example:

- Does Alex have a partner or a child of his own?
- Is he receiving any benefits in his own right (like Universal Credit or Income Support)?
- Are there any other children in your household you'd like to ask about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. Alex doesn't have a partner or children. He's not getting any benefits in his own name either - he's just living at home with me while he figures out what he wants to do next. It's just him I'm asking about.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: Child Benefit typically stops when a child turns 16, unless they continue in approved full-time non-advanced education or approved training. In those cases, it can continue until they turn 20 (or until they leave the education or training, whichever is earlier).

Since Alex is 18 and has finished school, and is not currently enrolled in any courses or approved training program, he doesn't meet the qualifying conditions for Child Benefit. Simply looking for work, unfortunately, doesn't qualify.

However, if Alex does decide to return to education or start an approved training course in the future, you may be able to claim Child Benefit for him again at that point - as long as he's under 20 when he starts.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about Child Benefit?
